tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

qise-two-training-levels: Section VII, p.21: the paper states in its own summary what its recommendations aim to enable (quantum aware and quantum proficient). Read in the summary paragraph; the quote is verbatim and the value matches it.
qise-paper-focus-undergraduate-gap: Section I, p.3: the paper states its own focus, set within K-12, Masters and workforce activities. The value matches the passage.
qise-modules-approach-and-labels: Section III, p.7 and the contents list: the paper states its modular design, the E and A labels, and lists Module 0 to Module 12. The value describes the paper's own proposed course, not a result.
qise-module-duration-1-3-weeks: Section III, p.7: the authors state the design assumption of 1-3 weeks per module in the paragraph that explains how modules combine into courses. It is their own envisioned design.
qise-modules-focus-on-computing: Section III, p.7: the authors state that the modules lean toward computing, with less on communication and sensing, and call for added modules. A limit of their own proposal.
qise-learning-goals-open-question: Section III, p.7: the authors state that learning goals based on the Key Concepts must still be developed and call it an open research question. A gap in their own proposal.
qise-module-5-nisq-content: Section III-F, p.8: the Module 5 text lists NISQ devices and heuristic algorithms (VQE, QAOA, possibly machine learning algorithms). It is the paper's own proposed content, stated in full.
qise-examples-not-best-programs: Section IV-D, pp.13-14: the authors state that the three example minors are working examples, not the only or best programs, and first attempts. They state this about their own examples.
qise-track-typical-structure: Section IV-E, p.14: the paper's own proposed track structure, stated in full. The value says 'propose' and matches the passage.
qise-dei-recommendation-categories: Section V-E, p.17: the paper states the three categories its own DEI recommendations fall into, and the following text goes through them. The value matches.
qise-workshop-community-input-basis: Section VII, p.22 acknowledgments: the authors state the NSF workshop feedback they drew on, with 480 attendees. It is the stated input basis of the paper; the value reports it as an acknowledgment.
qise-define-quantum-engineering: Section I, p.3: 'we define quantum engineering as ...', built on the National Quantum Initiative Act definition of QIS. The paper defines the term itself. Stored HIGH is supported.
qise-recommendations-scope: Section VII, p.22: the authors state that their recommendations reflect only the authors while drawing on community input. A statement of the paper's own scope. Stored HIGH is supported.
arch-modular-attention: Introduction: the paper states its own architecture (attention-based, modular, one trainable module per logical gate, joint tracking of correlations across logical qubits). The value states only the design and leaves out the performance claim in the same sentence.
output-per-qubit-marginal: Neural Decoder Architecture section: the paper defines the decoder's input (complete syndrome history) and output (per-qubit marginal probability of a logical error).
training-intermediate-supervision: Training Methodology (main text) and Methods: for n layers the authors simulate transversal measurements after each layer, giving n training examples per circuit. Both passages agree. Their own training setup.
training-on-the-fly-and-fingerprint: Training Methodology: circuits are sampled randomly during training and each logical qubit gets a per-shot random fingerprint embedding. The stated purpose (prevent position-dependent behavior) is the authors' own rationale in the same passage; the setup is what is settled.
model-size-and-embedding: Methods, architecture description: 13.6 million parameters in total and an embedding dimension of 384. Both numbers are stated in the paper's own model description.
five-models-trained: Methods, Training strategies paragraph: five models, with batch sizes and step counts per figure as listed. The value matches the passage.
fig1-simulation-setup: Methods, numerical simulation details: 20 random Clifford circuits per depth, multiple shots, ML decoder against an MLE decoder implemented with gurobi. The paper's own protocol.
fig1-noise-model: Methods, numerical simulation details: circuit-level depolarizing noise, p/15 per two-qubit error, p/10 for single-qubit gates, resets and measurements. The value matches the passage.
fig1-scope-limits: Methods, numerical simulation details: results are limited to CNOT circuits (SWAP supported but not reported), single-qubit gates drawn from I, X, Y, Z, H, and the analysis uses I, X, Z observables only. The paper states these limits itself.
fig1-error-rate-normalization: Methods: the reported logical error rate is the fraction of shots where the decoded parity differed from the true value of the target observable, normalized per round. The paper defines its metric.
logical-flip-label-and-loss: Methods, Loss definition: the logical flip is derived from tracked Pauli errors, needed when transversal outcomes are nondeterministic (for example most magic-state circuits), and training uses binary cross entropy. The paper defines its own label and loss.
loss-decoding-setup: Loss Decoding section: the paper states the circuit (a [[15,1,3]] Reed-Muller qubit with alternating transversal Cliffords and teleportation) and that lost qubits are detected by loss-resolving readout at each teleportation step.
loss-training-erasure-approximation: Loss Decoding section: the paper states the training approximation (loss as a fully depolarizing channel) and that inference simulates loss exactly. The 'well-justified' reason is the authors' own informal argument; the grade covers that the paper states the setup and its stated reason, not that the approximation is shown to be harmless.
cluster-state-simplification: Cluster-state section: the paper states its target circuits (1D and 2D cluster states from logical Steane codes), the observables (cluster-state logical stabilizers) and that it uses a CNN with kernel size three in place of the attention model. Its own design.
interpretability-limit: Section on interpretability (near Fig. 4): the authors state that their analyses capture only coarse correlation structure and that principled interpretability is future work. A limit of their own work.
code-family-scope-and-future-work: Discussion and Methods: the authors state the work covers surface, color and Reed-Muller codes, that qLDPC extension is future work, and that a full study of the GNN strategy is left for future work. A stated scope limit.
swp-problem-definition: Section I: the paper defines the SWP as scheduling social-worker visits under distance and time limits. The NP-class remark in the same sentence is a field characterization the paper carries with a citation; the definition is what the paper settles.
qcbr-proposal-design: Fig. 3 caption, Section on the quantum case-based system: the paper states that its qCBR replaces the retrieve and retain blocks with a variational classifier and the re-use and revise blocks with a VQE-based synthesis system. Its own proposed design.
qcbr-classifier-design: Fig. 5 caption and Appendix (fidelity cost function): data re-uploading classifier and a fidelity cost that maximizes average fidelity with the class state. The paper states its own classifier design. The cost function itself is cited from [15].
qcbr-test-sizes-and-qubits: Section V: all tests use n = 4 patients, an 8-dimensional vector, and q = log2(NSOL) = 3 qubits. The paper states these as its own test setup.
qcbr-class-count-rule: Section V, eq. (6): the class count of the classifier is defined by the equation under the conditions that every worker has a patient and workers are indistinguishable. A definition the paper gives for its own setup.
qcbr-evaluation-protocol: Section VI: test samples are VQE-solved schedules (ground truth), with leave-one-out cross-validation, and accuracy is correct labels over total labels. The paper's own protocol.
qcbr-overlap-preprocessing: Retain section and Section on results: ICA to reduce overlap, then PCA from 8 to 2 dimensions, and an experiment without ICA and PCA using an 8-dimensional classifier. The paper's own processing pipeline.
qcbr-overlap-source: Retain section: the paper states the 30 minute visit margin in the SWP data and the resulting overlap between schedules. It describes the paper's own dataset and the cause the authors give for the overlap.
qcbr-limit-initial-point-average: Discussion, 'aspects to refine' paragraph: the authors state that the system uses the average Initial point per class and that a better choice could still be made. A limit of their own system.
qcbr-limit-noise-generalize: Discussion: the authors list as remaining improvements training with noisy data and generalizing to other problem types by redesigning the case memory. Stated limits of their own work.
qcbr-future-quantum-ica-qram: Discussion: the authors name quantum ICA and a qRAM-based case memory as future work, so they are outside the paper's scope. The value says only this.
qcbr-case-memory-classical-ram: Fig. 7 and Fig. 8 captions: the qCBR memory structure is based on classical RAM. The paper states its own design.
fourier-model-definition: Section 'Our quantum model': the paper defines its model U = F V with a variational feature map and circuit. The 'can behave like a proper QNN' part is the authors' own aim, attributed in the value ('which they say'); the definition is what the paper settles.
hamiltonian-data-encoding: Section on the feature map: 'This work follows the data encoding Hamiltonians idea', followed by its description. The paper's own encoding choice.
classical-data-scope: Section A, Feature Map: 'This article deals exclusively with classical data.' The paper states its own scope.
pennylane-simulation-setup: Abstract: the paper states that all proposed models were performed and tested with Pennylane. The value matches.
observable-z-setup: Section D, The Observable: 'In our case, we use the computational basis Z.' The paper's own choice.
four-datasets-setup: Results, Classifiers: the paper states that it generated four datasets (crown, circle, square, SWP). The value matches.
interpolation-test-signals: Results, Trigonometric Interpolation: the input signals are sine, cosine, log, saw-tooth and square. The value matches.
fourier-series-assumption: Section 'Our model as a trigonometric interpolation': the paper states that, from its Section VI, it assumes f(x) has a Fourier series decomposition, and then assumes uniform convergence. A stated assumption of its own analysis.
cos-sin-simulation-aim: Section on Hamiltonian time evolution: the paper states that its test case is simulating cos(tx) and sin(tx). The value matches. It states the aim, not an outcome.
sample-rate-nyquist: Results, interpolation: 'We define sample rate frequency to accomplish a Nyquist theorem.' The passage is short but states the paper's own sampling choice, and the value claims no more.
high-frequency-decay-limit: Fig. 14 caption and Conclusion: the paper reports that the signal tail decays for a multiplied-frequency signal and the layer count must rise considerably, and the conclusion names this a limitation for the highest-frequency inputs. The paper states it as a limit of its own model.
fft-coefficient-method: Discussion: the paper states that it computed the Fourier coefficients by approximation and classical fft (figure 10) and that exact determination is very challenging. Both are its own method and stated limit.
coefficient-precision-open-problem: Conclusion: 'it remains a challenge to finish determining with greater precision the Fourier coefficients.' A limit the paper states about its own work.
fourier-intuition-not-proven: Discussion: the authors state that their intuition (rotation gates imply a Fourier series) is not demonstrated and that a demonstration is not trivial. A stated limit.
binary-classifier-sign-readout: Section on prediction (eq. 32 and the text): the binary classifier measures the expectation value and takes the sign. The paper's own readout.
no-complexity-study: Discussion: 'We have not made a detailed study of the algorithm's computational complexity.' A limit the paper states about its own work.
training-error-equation-5: Section C: equation (5) defines the mean squared error used to analyze training errors. The paper defines its own error measure.
code-availability: Code section: the paper states where its code is (GitHub repository pifparfait/Fourier_Based_QML). The value matches. It is a statement about the paper's own materials.
atchade-limits: Section E, Limitations: 'The qubits' scarcity and susceptibility to errors and decoherence significantly cap the complexity and size of the models we can reliably implement.' The authors state it about their own models. Stored HIGH is supported. The quote in the stored text uses a curly apostrophe; the sentence is verbatim in the paper.
arch-fully-connected-five-layer: Section on Methods: both models have five fully connected layers, with real weights and ReLU for the RVNN, complex weights and CReLU for the CVNN, and the CVNN parameter count capped at or below the RVNN's. The paper's own setup; Tables S1 and S2 list the sizes.
input-encoding-rvnn-cvnn: Methods: the paper defines the RVNN real decomposition of off-diagonal elements and the CVNN complex-vector encoding with the a -> a + ia embedding for diagonals, discarded at output.
hermiticity-by-construction: Methods: the upper-triangular representation recovers the lower triangle by conjugation, so Hermiticity holds by construction of the representation. This follows directly from the definition the paper gives.
cvnn-layer-definition: Methods, eqs. 11 and 12: the paper defines the CVNN layer and its real block form. The statement that the block form represents true complex multiplication follows from the equation.
initialisation-schemes: Methods and the initialization passage: He uniform for the RVNN with zero biases, and for the CVNN a variance of 1/n_in per component (total 2/n_in) with zero biases. The paper's own setup. Checked against eq. 15 and the bias sentences.
composite-loss-and-weights: Methods, eqs. 19-24: the composite loss with the four terms, and 'In all simulations reported here, we use alpha1 = alpha2 = 1.0, alpha3 = 2.0, alpha4 = 3.0'. The value matches.
sb-training-data: Methods, data section: QD3SET-1 spin-boson data with 1000 simulations (500 symmetric and 500 asymmetric) from HEOM, only the symmetric 500 used, 400 chosen by farthest point sampling for training, the rest for out-of-sample tests. The value matches. Note that the Supporting Information describes the same set as 1000 trajectories per parameter combination, which reads differently; the value reports the main text.
fmo-training-data: Methods, data section: 7-site and 8-site data from QD3SET-1 (sites 1 and 6, plus site 8), 500 simulations per excitation scenario, LTLME propagation, and self-generated 4-site data with site 1 excitation. The value matches.
trajectory-length-and-windows: Methods and training section: SB trajectories of 20/Delta with dt = 0.05, FMO dynamics 2 ps with 0.005 ps steps, and 81 input steps with 40 (SB) or 80 (FMO) predicted. The value matches the main text. The Supporting Information gives a longer FMO propagation (50 ps, 5 fs) for the source data, which is a separate item.
training-protocol-si: Methods and Table S1: 10^5 epochs (the exponent is flat in the text layer, confirmed by 100000 in Table S1), Adam, learning rate 1e-3. The value matches.
parameter-counts-and-widths: Methods and Table S1 caption: the architectures and parameter counts are tabulated in the Supporting Information and the CVNN count is capped at or below the RVNN's. The value states only that, and the passage supports it.
ohmic-setup: Supporting Information S5: 500 trajectories for site 1 excitation, 400 for training by farthest point sampling and 100 reserved for testing. The value matches.
scope-bath-and-systems: Methods and Section on results: Debye spectral density for SB and FMO with identical parameters across sites, and an Ohmic spectral density only for the 8-site FMO (SI S5). No other bath appears in the text. The 'only other bath' wording is an inference from that, and the text supports it.
sb-and-fmo-parameter-grids-si: Supporting Information S2: SB dataset of 1000 trajectories per parameter combination, t_Delta = 20 with dt = 0.05, and FMO propagation to 50 ps with 5 fs. The value matches the SI. It differs from the main text (2 ps, 0.005 ps), which describes the training window, not the source data.
fmo-grid-and-fps: Supporting Information S2: the 500 most distant parameter combinations from the stated grids, and the farthest point sampling rule (eq. 5). The paper states its own sampling grids and the algorithm.
code-and-data-availability: End of the main text: the authors state that code and data are at the GitHub repository Arif-PhyChem/cvnn. The value matches.

theory_low.cluster-state-error-locality: Cluster-state section: the short-range claim comes from a two-sentence informal argument about how Z and X errors propagate through CZ gates. There is no theorem, lemma or proof, and it is used as motivation for the CNN. An argued claim, not a proved result.
